sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability focuses on a specific condition.
Visualize this as zooming into subset B.
We measure how much of A overlaps within B.
animations: Fade in a Dot representing event A [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg].
Fade in a Square representing event B.
Show intersection Dot-Square with color #FFFF00.
Flash conditional probability P(A|B) text formula.
Highlight P(A|B) = P(A∩B) / P(B) in #00FF00 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnifier.svg].

sections.title: The Definition of Independence
lecture_lines: Independence means events don't influence each other.
P(A|B) equals P(A) if A and B are independent.
Knowing B gives zero new information about A.
animations: Show two independent event circles A and B, representing outcomes like a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg].
Show P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B) with #FFFFFF color.
Flash the equality to emphasize independence.
Highlight the formula P(A|B) = P(A) in #FF00FF.
Draw a box around the independence definition, potentially involving a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dice.svg].

sections.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem: Updating Beliefs
lecture_lines: Bayes' theorem bridges P(A|B) and P(B|A).
It updates our prior beliefs using new evidence.
Imagine a robot updating its hunt for a target.
New rustling (evidence) changes the fox probability.
animations: Display P(H|E) = P(E|H)P(H) / P(E). [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg]
Break down P(H|E) and P(E|H) labels in #00FFFF.
Animate P(H) prior updating to posterior.
Show normalization constant P(E) in #FF0000.
Display final update logic clearly. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg]

sections.title: Synthesis: Bayes vs. Independence
lecture_lines: What happens if events are independent?
Bayes' theorem simplifies to a standard identity.
Independence is just a special, simple case.
animations: Place Bayes formula in grid D3.
Place Independence formula in grid D4.
Draw arrow between formulas highlighting differences.

sections.title: Practical Application: The Diagnostic Test
lecture_lines: Let's apply this to a medical test.
A rare virus requires calculating posterior probability.
The low base rate can cause false positives.
Bayes' theorem reveals the truth behind test results.
Probability updates our understanding of the patient's state.
animations: Display patient [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/patient.svg] test scenario with probability tree.
Apply Bayes formula to calculate P(Disease|Positive) given the presence of virus [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/virus.svg].
Show the result prominently in #00FF00.
